title: fix(plugin-designer): MetadataFieldsPage renders a spec-refused save's issues through the one shared reader (objectui#11302)
body:
Fixes #11302

Clause-②: yes

## What this changes

- **`@object-ui/data-objectstack`** gains the one reader of a failed metadata save, in a new module `src/metadata-error.ts` beside the `MetadataError` and `MetadataValidationIssue` it reads. Two new barrel exports: `formatMetadataError(err)` (one line per structured issue, otherwise the error's own message) and `formatMetadataIssue(issue)` (that one-line grammar). `extractIssues` moves too but stays module-level, because no caller outside the module uses it. The code moved unchanged from app-shell's `views/studio-design/metadataError.ts`.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-designer` `MetadataFieldsPage`**: both of its catch paths (load and save) now set the banner from `formatMetadataError(err)` instead of `err.message`. A spec-refused save shows each issue on its own line, naming the field and the fix, for example `• fields.Bad Name — Field names must be lowercase snake_case (…)`. Every other failure still shows its own message. That includes the page's own pre-request refusals from `toFieldsMap`.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell`**: `ObjectHooksPanel`, `PackageOwdOverviewPanel` and `StudioDesignSurface` import `formatMetadataError` from `@object-ui/data-objectstack`. `metadataError.ts` keeps only the publish formatter (`formatPublishFailures`, `PublishFailure`, `BATCH_ABORTED_CODE`), which now writes each issue with `formatMetadataIssue`. ⛔ No second issue formatter anywhere.
- The reader's unit tests moved with it to `packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-error.test.ts`, with the cases unchanged plus one for `formatMetadataIssue`. App-shell's test file keeps the publish formatter's cases.
- `packages/data-objectstack/README.md` gets a short "Showing a Refused Metadata Save" section.
- Three changesets: `data-objectstack` **minor** (two new exports, additive), `plugin-designer` patch, and `app-shell` patch (what it shows is unchanged).

## Why

objectstack's `/meta` write doors answer a spec-refused save with `422 INVALID_METADATA`. On those faces the error's message is a headline: a count plus `path [code]` locators (`metadata-protocol`'s `specValidationFindings`). The author's prescription rides in the structured issues instead, and `MetadataClient` puts those on `err.issues`. The page showed `err.message` only, so it showed the headline and never the remedy.

## The dispatch's Zone 2, measured

1. **Red reproduced first, as the card describes.** I tested the real `MetadataFieldsPage`, the real `FieldDesigner`, the real `DrawerForm` (with the name typed into its input and its submit pressed) and a real `MetadataClient`. The fetch double runs the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 `ObjectSchema` and answers the dispatcher's 422 envelope. On `c82ff391f7`, saving `Bad Name` showed only the headline, and the PUT carried `["name","Bad Name"]`. One harness difference from the card: `ObjectGrid` is the designer suite's grid mock, kept only for its "Add" button, because the grid is not on the save path. My double also follows the server's `zodIssuesToMetadataIssues` container descent. So `Bad Name` gives two issues: the `invalid_key` wrapper ("Invalid key in record") and the `invalid_format` issue below it, which carries the snake_case prescription. The card's headline read "1 issue".
2. **Where the reader lives: dependency graph.** `@object-ui/app-shell` depends on `@object-ui/plugin-designer` (a dependency and a peer), so plugin-designer cannot import app-shell. Both depend on `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, which owns `MetadataError.issues`, so the reader lives there and is exported once. App-shell keeps **no** re-export. The old module is not in the app-shell barrel. A `git grep` for its symbols outside `packages/app-shell` finds only changeset prose and an unrelated local variable named `metadataError` in `AppContent.tsx`.
   - **The two app-shell surfaces do not use the same reader today.** `ResourceEditPage` never called `formatMetadataError`. It reads `err.body.issues`, which is the REST face's top-level array, maps it into inline `SchemaForm` field errors with `translateValidationMessage`, and holds the refused slices. That is a different rendering, not a banner formatter, so I did **not** converge it. Doing so would need a public export of `extractIssues`, and it is outside this card's file list. Its extraction has a measured consequence, reported under "Out of scope" below.
3. **What the page renders.** It renders the same lines the studio-design surfaces render: `• PATH — MESSAGE` per issue, with `(root)` for an empty path, joined by newlines. The banner was already a `pre` element with `whitespace-pre-wrap`, so each newline shows as a line. A pin asserts the element and the class, and a JSX comment on the element now says why.
4. **`Clause-②`.** It stays **yes**: the reader is a new published export of `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, with a `minor` changeset.

Zone 1 is followed as ruled. A `__proto__` save shows its prescription. `constructor` / `prototype` still give a field-less issue at `fields` until objectstack#20997 lands. The pin records today's reading and renders whatever path it is given, so when that lands only the instrument line moves.

## Pins

`packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.refusalIssues-11302.test.tsx` uses the harness from Zone 2 item 1:

- **instrument**: what the installed spec says about each probe name (`Bad Name` at `fields.Bad Name` plus the nested snake_case prescription; `__proto__` at `fields.__proto__` with "Rename the key"; `constructor` at `fields` today).
- `Bad Name`, `__proto__` and `constructor`: the banner is **byte-for-byte** the shared reader's output over the issues the gate sent, the prescription text is on screen, and the banner is not the headline.
- the multi-line list keeps its newlines (two lines, in a `pre` element with `whitespace-pre-wrap`).
- **controls**: a valid name (`good_name`) passes the same gate and saves with no banner, and a 503 that carries no issues still shows its own message.

## Tests (all at HEAD `a1eb87fa39`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-designer/ packages/data-objectstack/ packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/__tests__/` gave **`Test Files 221 passed (221)` · `Tests 1935 passed (1935)`**, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The last path covers `AiChatPage`, a `formatPublishFailures` consumer. A `git grep -l` for `formatMetadataError` / `extractIssues` finds no app-shell suite outside `studio-design/`.
- Builds: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-designer^...' --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` gave `28 successful, 28 total`. I ran it through turbo rather than `pnpm --filter … build` so that a cap-killed run could resume from cache. It is the same closure. I then ran the doc-snippet gate's own `--build-filter` closure, which gave `35 successful, 35 total`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack --filter @object-ui/plugin-designer --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` gave all three `Done`, exit 0. `--listFiles` confirms that each package's type-check program includes the new or edited test file. The rebuilt `data-objectstack/dist/index.d.ts` carries both new exports (3 hits), so the consumers were type-checked against the new declarations rather than a stale cache.

### Ablation (the pin can fail)

`node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs --file packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.tsx --anchor 'error: formatMetadataError(err),' --replacement 'error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),' --expect 2 -- … vitest run …refusalIssues-11302.test.tsx`. This puts back the exact pre-fix catch on both paths.

- The mutation landed: anchor `x2 → x0`, replacement `x0 → x2`, blob `e91b2064378f → 79d4ead2c6f8`.
- The run went red as expected: **`Tests 4 failed | 5 passed (9)`**. The three refusal cases plus the multi-line case failed, each one receiving the headline (for example `object/probe_widget failed spec validation: 1 issue — fields.__proto__ [custom]`). The instrument and both controls stayed green.
- Restore: `blob == HEAD (e91b2064378f)` and `git diff HEAD` empty.
- The test imports the page by relative path and `@object-ui/data-objectstack` through the root vitest alias to `src`, so no `dist` was involved in this ablation.

| `pnpm changeset:check` | three `✅` lines, including `No changeset declares a major bump` · exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | `✅ OK` · exit 0, and the self-scan of the 14 changed files with `grep -naP` found 0 hits |

Not measured: the repo-wide `pnpm lint` / `pnpm test`, which CI runs.

## Acceptance notes

- `@object-ui/app-shell`'s `PackagesPage` builds its own publish-failure message: the causal item's `error`, through i18n strings, without the causal item's `issues`. It does not use `formatPublishFailures`. This is an observation and was not measured on screen. Possible carrier: whoever next edits `PackagesPage`'s publish action. Carrier today: none.
- No `content/docs/guide` page covers `MetadataClient` save errors, so only the package README was updated.

## Out of scope (reported to the seat, not filed by this dev)

- **class (a): `ResourceEditPage` shows `[object Object]` for a spec-refused save on the HTTP dispatcher face.** **Reach:** the named real producer is objectstack `@objectstack/runtime`'s meta save branch (write face `meta-dispatch`). It answers through `errorFromThrown`, so the issues ride in `error.details.issues` and `error` is an object. **Measured** with a throwaway probe, not committed, on the real `MetadataResourceEditPage` from the `serverRefusalGate` harness. The probe threw the error `MetadataClient` builds from that envelope. On screen: `[object Object]`; the Save title read `The server refused this draft — fix  before saving.` (the field label is empty); the prescription sentinel was absent. Control, using the REST-face shape (top-level `issues`, `error` a string) on the same harness: the issue message is shown, and the title names `regions → main → components → offender → visibleWhen`. **Mechanism:** that branch reads `err.body.issues` instead of `err.issues`, then falls back to `String(err.body.error)`. Dedupe words: `ResourceEditPage object Object 422` · `dispatcher details.issues ResourceEditPage` · `metadata-admin refused save banner`.
